title: 6 ways to be more persuasive
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】增強說服力的 6 種方法（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: You can’t give a powerful new idea to an audience unless you can learn how to explain it.
cues.en: You can’t give a powerful new idea to an audience unless you can learn how to explain it.
cues.zh: 除非你能學會如何解釋它，否則你無法向觀眾提供一個強而有力的新想法。

cues.text: Each step builds on what the listener already knows, and metaphors and examples help show how the idea is pieced together.
cues.en: Each step builds on what the listener already knows, and metaphors and examples help show how the idea is pieced together.
cues.zh: 每個步驟都建立在聽眾已經知道的基礎上，隱喻和例子有助於展示這個想法是如何拼湊在一起的。

cues.text: But if explanation is building a brand new idea in someone’s mind,
cues.en: But if explanation is building a brand new idea in someone’s mind,
cues.zh: 但如果解釋是在某人的腦海中建立一個全新的想法，

cues.text: persuasion is something a little more.
cues.en: persuasion is something a little more.
cues.zh: 說服是更多的事情。

cues.text: Persuasion means convincing an audience that their way of seeing something—
cues.en: Persuasion means convincing an audience that their way of seeing something—
cues.zh: 說服意味著讓觀眾相信他們看待事物的方式——

cues.text: their perspective— isn’t quite right.
cues.en: their perspective— isn’t quite right.
cues.zh: 他們的觀點——不太正確。

cues.text: That means taking down the parts of their thinking that aren't working and rebuilding something better.
cues.en: That means taking down the parts of their thinking that aren't working and rebuilding something better.
cues.zh: 這意味著消除他們思維中不起作用的部分並重建更好的東西。

cues.text: Psychologist Barry Schwartz gave a talk that changed the way
cues.en: Psychologist Barry Schwartz gave a talk that changed the way
cues.zh: 心理學家巴里·施瓦茨（Barry Schwartz）的演講改變了方式

cues.text: his audience thinks about choice.
cues.en: his audience thinks about choice.
cues.zh: 他的聽眾思考選擇。

cues.text: Many people are obsessed with maximizing choice; Schwartz sees things differently.
cues.en: Many people are obsessed with maximizing choice; Schwartz sees things differently.
cues.zh: 許多人沉迷於選擇最大化；施瓦茨有不同的看法。

cues.text: He gave a talk on what he calls “the paradox of choice.” Schwartz builds the surprising case that in many circumstances
cues.en: He gave a talk on what he calls “the paradox of choice.” Schwartz builds the surprising case that in many circumstances
cues.zh: 他發表了一場關於他所謂的「選擇悖論」的演講。施瓦茨建立了一個令人驚訝的案例，在許多情況下

cues.text: having too many choices actually makes people unhappy.
cues.en: having too many choices actually makes people unhappy.
cues.zh: 選擇太多其實會讓人不快樂。

cues.text: Author Elizabeth Gilbert did something similar.
cues.en: Author Elizabeth Gilbert did something similar.
cues.zh: 作家伊莉莎白·吉爾伯特也做了類似的事情。

cues.text: She showed how the power of storytelling can help persuade an audience
cues.en: She showed how the power of storytelling can help persuade an audience
cues.zh: 她展示了講故事的力量如何幫助說服觀眾

cues.text: of a new idea.
cues.en: of a new idea.
cues.zh: 一個新想法。

cues.text: Her goal was to change the way they thought about creative genius.
cues.en: Her goal was to change the way they thought about creative genius.
cues.zh: 她的目標是改變他們對創意天才的看法。

cues.text: Instead of imagining genius as something people are born with— either you have it or you don’t—
cues.en: Instead of imagining genius as something people are born with— either you have it or you don’t—
cues.zh: 不要把天才想像成人們與生俱來的東西——要麼有，要麼沒有——

cues.text: she wanted to persuade her audience to think of it as something people receive as a gift from time to time.
cues.en: she wanted to persuade her audience to think of it as something people receive as a gift from time to time.
cues.zh: 她想說服觀眾將其視為人們時不時收到的禮物。

cues.text: Gilbert used her brilliance as a storyteller to persuade her audience
cues.en: Gilbert used her brilliance as a storyteller to persuade her audience
cues.zh: 吉爾伯特利用她講故事的才華來說服觀眾

cues.text: of this idea.
cues.en: of this idea.
cues.zh: 這個想法。

cues.text: She also showed them the term “genius” was viewed differently in history.
cues.en: She also showed them the term “genius” was viewed differently in history.
cues.zh: 她也向他們展示了歷史上對「天才」一詞的不同看法。

cues.text: It wasn't always thought of as a thing a person was.
cues.en: It wasn't always thought of as a thing a person was.
cues.zh: 它並不總是被認為是一個人。

cues.text: It used to be thought of as something that came to them.
cues.en: It used to be thought of as something that came to them.
cues.zh: 它曾經被認為是降臨到他們身上的東西。

cues.text: If you're giving a talk that requires persuading an audience to see something differently,
cues.en: If you're giving a talk that requires persuading an audience to see something differently,
cues.zh: 如果你的演講需要說服聽眾以不同的方式看待某些事情，

cues.text: the key is to take the journey one step at a time.
cues.en: the key is to take the journey one step at a time.
cues.zh: 關鍵是一步一步地走下去。

cues.text: Prime your listener’s mind for a change.
cues.en: Prime your listener’s mind for a change.
cues.zh: 讓聽眾的思想做好改變的準備。

cues.text: The philosopher Daniel Dennett uses the term “intuition pump”
cues.en: The philosopher Daniel Dennett uses the term “intuition pump”
cues.zh: 哲學家丹尼爾·丹尼特使用術語“直覺泵”

cues.text: to refer to any language that makes a new idea seem more believable.
cues.en: to refer to any language that makes a new idea seem more believable.
cues.zh: 指任何使新想法看起來更可信的語言。

cues.text: In Barry Schwartz’s talk, “Paradox of Choice,” a shopping story he uses is an example of an intuition pump
cues.en: In Barry Schwartz’s talk, “Paradox of Choice,” a shopping story he uses is an example of an intuition pump
cues.zh: 在巴里·施瓦茨 (Barry Schwartz) 的演講「選擇悖論」中，他使用的一個購物故事就是直覺泵的一個例子

cues.text: that primes his audience’s mind for a change: So I went to replace my jeans after years and years of wearing these old ones.
cues.en: that primes his audience’s mind for a change: So I went to replace my jeans after years and years of wearing these old ones.
cues.zh: 這讓他的觀眾做好了改變的準備：所以在穿了很多年的舊牛仔褲之後，我去換掉了我的牛仔褲。

cues.text: And I said, “I want a pair of jeans, here’s my size.” And the shopkeeper said, “do you want slim fit, easy fit, relaxed fit?
cues.en: And I said, “I want a pair of jeans, here’s my size.” And the shopkeeper said, “do you want slim fit, easy fit, relaxed fit?
cues.zh: 我說：「我想要一條牛仔褲，這是我的尺寸。」店主說：「你想要修身款、寬鬆款、寬鬆款嗎？

cues.text: Do you want button fly or zipper fly?
cues.en: Do you want button fly or zipper fly?
cues.zh: 您想要紐帶門襟還是拉鍊門襟？

cues.text: You want stonewashed or acid washed? Do you want them distressed?
cues.en: You want stonewashed or acid washed? Do you want them distressed?
cues.zh: 您想要石洗還是酸洗？你想讓他們難受嗎？

cues.text: Do you want bootcut? Do you want tapered?” On and on he went. My jaw dropped.
cues.en: Do you want bootcut? Do you want tapered?” On and on he went. My jaw dropped.
cues.zh: 你想要引導嗎？你想要錐形嗎？ 」他不停地走。我的下巴都掉下來了。

cues.text: And after I recovered I said, “I want the kind that used to be the only kind.”
cues.en: And after I recovered I said, “I want the kind that used to be the only kind.”
cues.zh: 當我康復後，我說：“我想要以前唯一的那種。”

cues.text: Once an audience has been primed, it’s much easier to make your main argument.
cues.en: Once an audience has been primed, it’s much easier to make your main argument.
cues.zh: 一旦聽眾做好準備，你就更容易提出主要論點。

cues.text: Even if it contradicts an idea the audience held true.
cues.en: Even if it contradicts an idea the audience held true.
cues.zh: 即使它與觀眾所堅持的想法相矛盾。

cues.text: Another powerful tool is reason.
cues.en: Another powerful tool is reason.
cues.zh: 另一個強大的工具是理性。

cues.text: By using reasoning, you can show how and why something is true.
cues.en: By using reasoning, you can show how and why something is true.
cues.zh: 透過使用推理，您可以展示某件事如何以及為什麼是正確的。

cues.text: Each true assumption leads to a conclusion that must then also be true.
cues.en: Each true assumption leads to a conclusion that must then also be true.
cues.zh: 每個正確的假設都會得出一個結論，也必須是正確的。

cues.text: Reasoning works using the tool “if, then.” If X is true, then clearly Y must be true.
cues.en: Reasoning works using the tool “if, then.” If X is true, then clearly Y must be true.
cues.zh: 使用“如果，那麼”工具進行推理。如果 X 為真，那麼顯然 Y 一定為真。

cues.text: Another kind of reasoned argument is the detective story.
cues.en: Another kind of reasoned argument is the detective story.
cues.zh: 另一種理性論證是偵探故事。

cues.text: Some of the most persuasive TED Talks are set up like detective stories.
cues.en: Some of the most persuasive TED Talks are set up like detective stories.
cues.zh: 一些最具說服力的 TED 演講就像偵探故事一樣。

cues.text: You start with the big mystery, then travel the world of ideas in search of possible solutions to it,
cues.en: You start with the big mystery, then travel the world of ideas in search of possible solutions to it,
cues.zh: 你從一個大謎團開始，然後遊歷思想世界尋找可能的解決方案，

cues.text: ruling them out one by one, until there’s only one solution left.
cues.en: ruling them out one by one, until there’s only one solution left.
cues.zh: 將它們一一排除，直到只剩下一種解決方案。

cues.text: A simple example is artist Siegfried Woldhek’s talk.
cues.en: A simple example is artist Siegfried Woldhek’s talk.
cues.zh: 一個簡單的例子是藝術家 Siegfried Woldhek 的演講。

cues.text: He wanted to prove that three famous drawings by Leonardo da Vinci were actually self-portraits da Vinci made of himself
cues.en: He wanted to prove that three famous drawings by Leonardo da Vinci were actually self-portraits da Vinci made of himself
cues.zh: 他想證明達文西的三幅著名畫作其實是達文西為自己畫的自畫像

cues.text: at different stages of his life.
cues.en: at different stages of his life.
cues.zh: 在他人生的不同階段。

cues.text: He started with all of the 120 portraits of males
cues.en: He started with all of the 120 portraits of males
cues.zh: 他從全部 120 幅男性肖像開始

cues.text: that Leonardo is thought to have made and asks: were any of these self-portraits?
cues.en: that Leonardo is thought to have made and asks: were any of these self-portraits?
cues.zh: 據信是李奧納多創作的，他問道：這些是自畫像嗎？

cues.text: Then, like a detective eliminating suspects, Woldhek cut them down.
cues.en: Then, like a detective eliminating suspects, Woldhek cut them down.
cues.zh: 然後，就像偵探消滅嫌疑人一樣，沃爾德赫克將他們消滅了。

cues.text: Finally, only three remained.
cues.en: Finally, only three remained.
cues.zh: 最後只剩下三個了。

cues.text: The remaining three portraits are of men of different ages and painted at different times,
cues.en: The remaining three portraits are of men of different ages and painted at different times,
cues.zh: 其餘三幅肖像畫則是不同年齡、不同時期的男性肖像，

cues.text: but they all share the same facial features.
cues.en: but they all share the same facial features.
cues.zh: 但他們都有相同的面部特徵。

cues.text: And they all match the facial features of a statue— the only known image of da Vinci made by someone else.
cues.en: And they all match the facial features of a statue— the only known image of da Vinci made by someone else.
cues.zh: 它們都與雕像的面部特徵相匹配——這是唯一已知的由別人製作的達文西雕像。

cues.text: What makes the detective story persuasive is that we feel as if we have gone on the same learning journey
cues.en: What makes the detective story persuasive is that we feel as if we have gone on the same learning journey
cues.zh: 偵探故事之所以有說服力，是因為我們感覺好像我們都在經歷同樣的學習旅程

cues.text: as the speaker.
cues.en: as the speaker.
cues.zh: 作為演講者。

cues.text: It can sometimes be hard to make reason-based talks really exciting to listen to.
cues.en: It can sometimes be hard to make reason-based talks really exciting to listen to.
cues.zh: 有時很難讓基於理性的演講真正令人興奮。

cues.text: Most people can be convinced by reason, but it doesn't always leave them feeling energized.
cues.en: Most people can be convinced by reason, but it doesn't always leave them feeling energized.
cues.zh: 大多數人都可以被理性所說服，但這並不總是讓他們感到充滿活力。

cues.text: So if you plan to use reason to persuade your audience, you may have to pick up some other tools as well:
cues.en: So if you plan to use reason to persuade your audience, you may have to pick up some other tools as well:
cues.zh: 因此，如果您打算用理性說服觀眾，您可能還需要選擇其他一些工具：

cues.text: 1. Inject some humor early on.
cues.en: 1. Inject some humor early on.
cues.zh: 1. 儘早注入一些幽默感。

cues.text: This says you're going to do some tough thinking, but we're going to have fun.
cues.en: This says you're going to do some tough thinking, but we're going to have fun.
cues.zh: 這表示你將進行一些艱難的思考，但我們會享受樂趣。

cues.text: 2. Add an anecdote.
cues.en: 2. Add an anecdote.
cues.zh: 2.增加一個軼事。

cues.text: You could tell an anecdote that shows how you became interested in the topic you've chosen.
cues.en: You could tell an anecdote that shows how you became interested in the topic you've chosen.
cues.zh: 你可以講一個軼事來表明你是如何對你選擇的主題感興趣的。

cues.text: 3. Offer vivid examples that ignite the audience’s imagination.
cues.en: 3. Offer vivid examples that ignite the audience’s imagination.
cues.zh: 3. 提供生動的例子，激發觀眾的想像。

cues.text: 4. Include third-party validation.
cues.en: 4. Include third-party validation.
cues.zh: 4. 包括第三方驗證。

cues.text: Pull in the opinions of other people who also believe your idea.
cues.en: Pull in the opinions of other people who also believe your idea.
cues.zh: 聽取其他也相信你的想法的人的意見。

cues.text: Persuasive talks that use reason may be harder for an audience to understand
cues.en: Persuasive talks that use reason may be harder for an audience to understand
cues.zh: 使用理由的說服性演講可能更難讓聽眾理解

cues.text: than other talks, and they may not be the most popular.
cues.en: than other talks, and they may not be the most popular.
cues.zh: 與其他演講相比，它們可能不是最受歡迎的。

cues.text: However, they are extremely important.
cues.en: However, they are extremely important.
cues.zh: 然而，它們非常重要。

cues.text: A strong, well-reasoned argument, even if it isn't immediately accepted by everyone,
cues.en: A strong, well-reasoned argument, even if it isn't immediately accepted by everyone,
cues.zh: 一個強有力的、有理有據的論點，即使它沒有立即被所有人接受，

cues.text: will gradually attract supporters until it becomes unstoppable.
cues.en: will gradually attract supporters until it becomes unstoppable.
cues.zh: 會逐漸吸引支持者，直到勢不可擋。
